title: A Practical AI Workflow
bullets: Our AI tools throughout: Gemini and Antigravity, using free accounts
Gemini: plan the page, draft content and guide the design
Antigravity: build, preview and improve the website
Plan: define the audience, purpose and approved facts
Design: choose a clear structure and readable appearance
Build: ask AI to create the page and open the preview
Review: check facts, mobile layout and links
Deploy: make the reviewed website available online
Repeat: brief -> draft -> check -> improve

title: Better Prompts with RCTFC
bullets: Role: who should AI act as?
Context: who is the website for, and why?
Task: what should AI produce?
Format: how should the answer be organized?
Constraints: what must AI include, avoid or verify?
Treat RCTFC as a practical checklist; review the actual answer

title: From a Vague Request to a Useful Brief
bullets: Vague: "Make me a professional website."
Role: "Act as a website content planner."
Context: "Use Mahfoudh Arous’s public LinkedIn profile as the source for his personal website and portfolio."
Task: "Draft a concise one-page personal website and portfolio outline."
Format: "Return a table of sections and suggested copy."
Constraints: "Use only supplied facts. Mark missing information. Do not invent credentials, clients or contact details."

title: Reuse Your Instructions: Skills & Gems
bullets: Save a short instruction checklist for tasks you repeat
Example: "Use approved facts, write concise copy, flag missing information and check the result."
Builder equivalent: a Skill packages reusable instructions and resources
Save your checklist in a note or a Gemini Gem
Reuse the same checklist when you draft another website brief

title: Quick Quiz: Which Instruction Helps Most?
bullets: Goal: reduce invented professional claims
A: "Make my profile sound impressive."
B: "Use only supplied facts and clearly mark missing information."
C: "Add convincing client testimonials."
Vote A, B or C in the poll or chat
Discuss: what should you still check in the AI's answer?

title: Live Demo: From My LinkedIn Profile to My Portfolio
bullets: LinkedIn: Profile → Resources → Save to PDF; upload to Gemini to extract experience, skills and projects
Website goal: help visitors understand my professional work
Approve the copy before building the page
Do not invent qualifications, projects, results or testimonials
Include your confirmed public profile link alongside the PDF or copied text

title: Design & Build One Clear Page
bullets: Approve the copy before generating the website
Use supported sections: introduction, experience/skills or services, projects, about and next step
Choose readable text, clear spacing and one main accent color
Ask AI to build a responsive page using the approved content
Open the preview and test the page
A design image is a reference; a website must contain usable text and links

title: Review, Improve & Check Again
bullets: Are all statements supported by the supplied profile?
Is the text readable on a phone?
Do navigation and approved links work?
Can you move through interactive elements with a keyboard?
Avoid private information, exposed credentials and pretend contact forms
What would make this page more useful to its visitors?
Request one specific revision, then repeat the affected checks

title: Git, GitHub & Deploying Your Website
bullets: Git: save versions of your project locally and track changes
GitHub: keep a project repository online
GitHub Pages: publish a static website from a repository
Local preview and public website are different stages
Browser route: upload index.html and style.css -> Pages settings -> deployment status -> public URL
Open and check the online version; a deployment attempt is not proof of success
Protect existing websites and never upload secrets or private files
No terminal needed for this route; use a separate project repository

title: Mini Challenge: Write Your Website Brief
bullets: Choose: portfolio, service page or small-business website
2 minutes: identify your audience and the action visitors should take
4 minutes: adapt the chat template or an example; start with Context, Task and one Constraint
Include: page sections, desired format and limits on invented information
3 minutes: discuss two volunteer examples
1 minute: choose one improvement to your brief
Use chat or paper; no account or installation is required

title: What’s Next? Topics to Explore
bullets: Connectors: give AI access to selected documents and tools with your permission
MCP (Model Context Protocol): a standard for connecting AI applications to tools and data
Automations: turn a useful AI task into a repeatable workflow
Working forms and databases: collect messages and store information
Custom domains, search visibility and analytics: help people find and use your website
Choose one topic to explore after you build and review your first page
